Re: Appeal of prior authorization denial for partial knee replacement  
Member: Rowan Carter  
Member ID: W914903090  
Procedure: Partial knee replacement, CPT 27446  
Reference number: POC-5BA41AD17E-24277  
Date of denial notice: August 19, 2026

Dear Aetna Member Appeals:

I appeal Aetna’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446, partial knee replacement. The denial states that the procedure does not meet the plan’s medical-necessity criteria. Based on the clinical records submitted with the authorization request, the requested unicompartmental knee arthroplasty is medically necessary.

Aetna’s publicly available Knee Arthroplasty Medical Clinical Policy Bulletin, policy number 0660, describes medical-necessity requirements for unicompartmental knee arthroplasty. I am not quoting the plan below; the following is an application of the clinical records to the policy criteria.

The records support the following:

1. Advanced disease limited to the medial compartment

The June 9, 2026 MRI documents full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medial osteoarthritis. This establishes severe structural disease in the medial compartment, the compartment targeted by the requested partial knee replacement.

2. Pain and functional disability

The patient has had nine months of progressive knee pain that has not improved with rest. The pain prevents climbing stairs without assistance and causes the patient to wake three to four times each night. The examination documents positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain. These findings demonstrate substantial pain and loss of function in daily activities.

3. Failure of conservative treatment

The patient completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy, including 16 visits from April 10, 2026, through July 17, 2026. The physical therapy discharge note documents this treatment and should satisfy the requirement for documented supervised therapy.

The patient also used NSAIDs for eight months with inadequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on June 17, 2026, produced only two weeks of partial relief. The clinical record therefore documents prolonged nonoperative treatment, including medication, injection treatment, supervised therapy, strengthening, and range-of-motion work, without adequate or durable improvement.

4. Absence of identified contraindications

The records document no active infection, BMI 29, and no smoking. They also document no untreated substance use. The available records do not identify a condition that would compromise implant stability, surgical recovery, or the ability to proceed with knee replacement.

The MRI and clinical presentation support a medial unicompartmental procedure rather than continued conservative management. The patient’s bone-on-bone medial disease, persistent symptoms, failed treatment, and significant functional impairment provide a clear medical basis for CPT 27446.

If Aetna believes additional information is needed regarding intact ligament stability, total knee arc of motion, the absence of deformity or subluxation, or the planned surgery date in relation to the June 17, 2026 injection, please identify each specific missing item and allow the treating surgeon to submit it. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery, can provide any additional examination findings or clarification needed. The denial should not be upheld without identifying the precise criterion that Aetna believes was not met and the clinical evidence supporting that conclusion.

Please overturn the denial and approve prior authorization for the requested partial knee replacement. If Aetna does not reverse the decision, please provide the complete clinical rationale, the specific criteria applied, the records relied upon, and instructions for any further internal or external review.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal.

Sincerely,

Rowan Carter
